Set DragDropOperationClass on a widget found by name in the tree of a Widget Blueprint, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step (set=true, changed=true, property_set); a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the class kept in memory. A widget already holding that class is left as it is (changed=false, saved=false, a note), nothing compiled or saved. Only list, tile and tree views (UListViewBase) have that property; any other widget gets set=false and a note, nothing written: its drag and drop is the OnDragDetected and OnDrop events of a User Widget graph, authored with build_blueprint_graph after list_overridable_functions. operation_class defaults to /Script/UMG.DragDropOperation; a class that does not load or is no UDragDropOperation, or a missing Blueprint or widget, is an error, nothing written. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Make the view with add_list_view (view_type List, Tile or Tree).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_blueprint_name` | string | yes | /Game path of the Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/UI/WBP_Inventory". |
| `widget_name` | string | yes | Name of the widget in the tree of that Blueprint, e.g. "ItemTiles"; only a list, tile or tree view can take the class. |
| `operation_class` | string | no | Class path of a UDragDropOperation subclass, e.g. "/Script/UMG.DragDropOperation" or "/Game/UI/DDO_Item.DDO_Item_C"; defaults to /Script/UMG.DragDropOperation. |

**Returns:** `{ widget_blueprint_name, widget_name, operation_class, set, changed, has_drag_drop_property, operation_class_loaded, property_set?, saved?, save_error?, note? }`

## `set_widget_navigation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Author a widget's GAMEPAD/KEYBOARD navigation rules -- what gets focus when the player pushes up, down, left, right, Tab or Shift+Tab off this widget. Without this a menu cannot be driven with a pad, and it is NOT reachable through set_widget_property: UWidget::Navigation is an Instanced SUBOBJECT that starts null, so there is no asset path a reflection setter could point at and a dotted path fails on a null segment. Follows the editor's own flow, including the two details that matter: the subobject is created RF_Transactional with template flags propagated, and if all six directions end up on Escape the subobject is DISCARDED (that is what tells "no navigation authored" apart from "navigation authored that happens to be the default", and it is what the Designer does). Read the result back with get_widget_blueprint_tree include_navigation=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_bp_path` | string | yes | /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset |
| `widget_name` | string | yes | Name of the widget in the tree whose navigation to author |
| `rules` | object | no | Dict of {direction: rule}. Direction is Up\|Down\|Left\|Right\|Next\|Previous (Next/Previous are Tab/Shift+Tab). The value is either a rule name string ("Wrap", "Stop", "Escape") or an object {"rule":"Explicit","widget_to_focus":"Btn_Confirm"} when the rule needs a target. Rules: Escape (default -- let the search continue outward), Stop (movement dies here), Wrap (cycle inside the container), Explicit (jump to widget_to_focus). |
| `all_directions` | string | no | Optional rule name applied to ALL SIX directions before `rules` is processed, so you can say "Stop everywhere, except Down" in one call. Explicit is refused here: it would need six different targets. |
| `save` | boolean | no | Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). |

**Returns:** `{ widget_bp_path, widget_name, applied: [{direction, rule, widget_to_focus}], current_navigation: {Up:{rule,widget_to_focus}, ...}, navigation_discarded: bool, saved, save_error } -- navigation_discarded:true means every direction ended on Escape so the subobject was dropped, exactly as the Designer does; current_navigation is then all-Escape.`

## `set_widget_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set ONE or MANY reflected properties on a widget of a Widget Blueprint, addressing NESTED STYLE FIELDS by dotted path ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor", "Items[0].Label") and reporting FIELD BY FIELD what landed, then compile and save it (save=false defers). Use it instead of set_properties for widgets: it finds the widget by name in the tree, writes leaf fields inside structs, takes color/margin/brush shorthands and compiles; set_properties takes only top-level names and compiles nothing. Two calling shapes over one write path: property_name+value, or a properties map under ONE Modify + ONE compile + ONE save (a FButtonStyle is ~30 leaf fields -- one call, not 30 recompiles). WARNING: the oracle is applied[]/ignored[]/errors[], NOT success: a key matching no reflected field lands in ignored[] and all_applied goes false. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. Read back with get_widget_blueprint_tree(property_paths=[...]); slot layout: set_slot_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_bp_path` | string | yes | /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset |
| `widget_name` | string | yes | name of the widget in the tree (get_widget_blueprint_tree lists them) |
| `property_name` | string | no | Single reflected property name ("Text") OR a dotted path into nested structs ("WidgetStyle.Normal.TintColor"); array indices are supported ("Items[0].Label"). Requires `value`. Omit when using `properties`. |
| `value` | any | no | New value for property_name: string, number, bool, JSON object (struct, applied field by field) or JSON array. Colors accept {"R":1,"G":0,"B":0,"A":1}, [r,g,b,a] or "#RRGGBBAA"; FMargin accepts a scalar, [h,v] or [l,t,r,b]; an FSlateBrush accepts a texture/material path string; enums accept the short name ("Box"). |
| `properties` | object | no | Batch form: {"&lt;dotted path>": &lt;value>, ...}. Every path is written against the SAME widget under one Modify/compile/save. Combinable with property_name+value (both end up in the same map). |
| `save` | boolean | no | Compile + save the Widget Blueprint when done (default true). Pass false to chain several calls and save once at the end -- the asset stays dirty in memory until something saves it. |

**Returns:** `{ widget_bp_path: string, widget_name: string, widget_class: string, requested_paths: [string], applied: [string], ignored: [string], errors: [{path, error}], failed_paths: [string], applied_count: int, all_applied: bool, current_values: object, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `stop_widget_animation`

*Destructive.*

Stop a widget animation. REAL stop (UUserWidget::StopAnimation) when a live PIE instance of this WidgetBP is found in the viewport's active UUserWidgets: stopped is true when the animation was playing before the call and is not after it; one that was not playing (stopped or paused) succeeds with stopped:false and a note, and one still playing after the call is an error. Falls back to an honest headless gate (stopped:false, headless:true, requires_pie:true) otherwise.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_bp_path` | string | yes | /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset |
| `animation_name` | string | yes | object name OR display label of the animation to stop |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). In a 2-player PIE session EVERY client has its OWN widgets, so the default may well read the other player's HUD. |

**Returns:** `{ widget_bp_path: string, animation_name: string, animation_exists: bool, stopped: bool, headless: bool, requires_pie: bool, note: string, saved: bool, live_widget_name?: string, live_animation_name?: string, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `unbind_widget_from_viewmodel`

*Destructive.*

Remove one binding from the MVVM view of a Widget Blueprint loaded by asset path, picked by binding_index or, when no index is given, by binding_id, then compile and save the Blueprint in one undo step; binding_count is what the view keeps. A binding that is not there (an index out of range, an id no binding has, or a Blueprint with no MVVM view: has_mvvm_extension=false) is a success with removed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is changed or saved. By index a repeat call removes the binding that moved into that index. Neither identifier, a binding_id that is not a GUID, or a missing Blueprint is an error. A failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Inverse: bind_widget_to_viewmodel; a whole context: remove_viewmodel.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_blueprint_name` | string | yes | /Game path of the Widget Blueprint asset |
| `binding_index` | number | no | int index of the binding to remove (primary identifier; one of binding_index / binding_id required) |
| `binding_id` | string | no | optional GUID string of the binding to remove (alternative to binding_index) |

**Returns:** `{ widget_blueprint_name, binding_index?, binding_id?, already_existed, removed, binding_count, has_mvvm_extension, saved, save_error?, note? }`
